interpretation: DET11107 retains a matching ball component at 5.682px, but an already present hand distractor grows and overtakes its component mass.
DET11501 retains the same peak near the ball; a small centroid shift changes error from 9.272px to 10.014px across the unchanged 10px boundary.
All four NFHS losses have weaker local response in every original contributor; each retains one contributor above 0.3, but its averaged local response is below 0.3.
All four recoveries cross the mean threshold upward. P00249 uses one contributor; that gain is not an averaging effect.
A surviving local response does not establish an accurate contributor component center. No alternate pooling or selection policy was tested.

limits: Failure/recovery-selected development context, not a causal test of overfitting or forgetting.
NFHS old caches bind original source/window/frame indices and model identity, not captured PNG or PTS hashes. New manifest provides source frame/PTS mapping.
Historical NFHS cache producer threshold 0.5 is retained; selection parity uses previously published strict 0.3 calibration.
Null or ineligible reference geometry remains null; no inferred centers.
Failed adaptation screen and retained expanded baseline remain unchanged.
Thirty-seven correlated development frames were selected around known losses/recoveries; this is not a fresh accuracy estimate.
No causal conclusion about NBA overfitting or catastrophic forgetting follows from this diagnostic.
TOR and protected NFHS holdouts/buffers remain untouched. Prior negative motion comparison and its pending three human reviews remain separate.
Generated reports, NPZ, figures, source footage and temporary helpers remain ignored.
